title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 52 (Order of performance of reciprocal promises)

content.overview: Section 52 provides that where the order in which reciprocal promises are to be performed is expressly fixed by the contract, they shall be performed in that order; and where the order is not expressly fixed by the contract, they shall be performed in that order which the nature of the transaction requires.
content.glance: Reciprocal promises: express order if fixed; otherwise order required by the nature of the transaction.
content.study: If the contract expressly fixes the order of reciprocal promises, they must be performed in that order. If not, they must be performed in the order which the nature of the transaction requires. Current-law framing: check for express order; if none, determine order from the nature of the transaction.

sections.heading: Expressly fixed order
sections.body: Where the order is expressly fixed by the contract, perform in that order.

sections.heading: Nature of the transaction
sections.body: Where not expressly fixed, perform in the order which the nature of the transaction requires.

provisions.title: Order of performance of reciprocal promises

examples.title: Work then payment
examples.body: A is to build a house for B and B is to pay on completion. The nature of the transaction requires A’s performance before B’s payment under s. 52.

hypotheticals.question: What if the contract is silent on order?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 52: perform in the order which the nature of the transaction requires.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-52
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Reciprocal promises may always be performed in any order the parties choose at the time.
misconceptions.correction: Section 52 requires the express contractual order or, failing that, the order required by the nature of the transaction.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 52 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Check for express order. II. If none, determine order from nature of transaction. III. Apply that order. IV. Conclude.

examTips: State both limbs: express order and nature of transaction.
